headline: Chip rout and Nvidia SEC probe report sink Nasdaq 5.3%; S&P 500 and Dow close in correction
summary: Stocks opened mixed, with the S&P 500 up as much as 0.3% and the Dow briefly higher, but selling in chip and AI names widened through the afternoon and the indexes closed near their lows. The damage was concentrated in mega-cap tech: the equal-weight S&P 500 fell about 2% versus 3.7% for the cap-weighted index, consumer staples was the only sector to rise, and the S&P 500 posted a seventh straight loss, its longest losing streak since February 2020, while the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for 2026.
drivers: The SOX fell about 10.7% and about 17% for the week, its worst since 2001, as worries about AI data-center spending, tighter US chip-export rules and unconfirmed reports of Google shifting custom-chip orders hit the group: AMD lost about 13%, Broadcom 12.2% and Micron about 13%, with memory names such as Western Digital and SanDisk also down double digits.
Nvidia plunges 14% on SEC accounting probe report

Nvidia was already down about 6–7% when Reuters reported that SEC enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues; it closed down 14% near $125.5, its seventh straight weekly loss and roughly $490 billion of market value erased in a day, adding to pressure after Jensen Huang's resignation.

Anthropic fell about 8.5% to $88.91 on its second day of trading, after dipping close to its $83 IPO price, as its debut and Nvidia's strong results this week failed to steady the AI trade; Intuit dropped more than 10% after cutting its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook and agreeing to sell Mailchimp.
Flight to safety in bonds and defensives

The 10-year yield fell about 14bp to 4.91%, its biggest one-day drop since Oct 22, and the 2-year about 17bp to 4.61%, trimming December hike odds slightly despite hawkish Fed talk; staples and health care held up (UnitedHealth and Humana rose on upgrades), while the VIX jumped 26% to 35.89 after touching 40 intraday.
week: For the week the S&P 500 fell 8.6%, the Nasdaq 10.0%, the Dow 8.0% and the Russell 2000 7.5%, the largest weekly losses since April 2025, while the 10-year yield dropped about 24bp and markets still price a December Fed hike.
watch: Next: a holiday-shortened week with Dell's results on Tue Nov 24, US markets shut for Thanksgiving on Thu Nov 26 and an early close on Fri Nov 27, then the Fed meeting on Dec 8–9.
